introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 14 shows how light is focused into a defective eye.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_11_fig_1.png)

(i) Name the eye defect experienced by the person.

(ii) State its possible causes and, using a diagram, show how it can be remedied.

(iii) If the near point of the eye is $2.0\ \mathrm{m}$, determine the power of the lens that will enable it to focus clearly a wall chart placed $1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ from the eye.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Eye defect.** In figure 14 the rays from a near object are brought to a focus **behind** the retina (beyond the eyeball). The defect is **hypermetropia (long-sightedness)**: near objects cannot be focused clearly.

**(ii) Causes and remedy.**

*Possible causes:* the eyeball is too short from front to back; or the eye lens or the cornea is too weak (too flat, focal length too long), for example because the ciliary muscles are weak or the lens has lost its elasticity with age.

*Remedy (diagram described):* a **converging (convex) lens**, in spectacles or a contact lens, is placed in front of the eye. In the diagram the rays from the near object, drawn from a point on the object, first meet the convex lens, which makes them less divergent (as if they came from a farther point, the near point of the eye); the eye lens then brings them to a focus **on the retina**. The diagram shows the object, the convex lens, the eye lens and the rays focused on the retina.

**(iii) Power of the lens.** The object (the chart) is at $u = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ and the lens must form a virtual image of it at the near point of the eye, $v = -2.0\ \mathrm{m}$ (on the same side as the object). With the real-is-positive convention,
$$\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{1.5} - \frac{1}{2.0} = 0.667 - 0.500 = 0.167\ \mathrm{m^{-1}},$$
so $f = +6.0\ \mathrm{m}$ and the power is
$$P = \frac{1}{f} = +0.17\ \mathrm{D}.$$
**A converging lens of power $+0.17\ \mathrm{D}$ (focal length $6.0\ \mathrm{m}$) is needed.**

**(i) Broken bone: X-rays.** Bone contains calcium, which has a high atomic number, so it **absorbs X-rays strongly**, whereas soft tissue absorbs them very little. The X-rays that pass through the body blacken a photographic plate (or a digital detector), so the bones show up as a clear shadow and a fracture appears as a dark line in the bone. Ultrasound is not suitable because it is almost completely reflected or absorbed by bone and cannot show what is inside it.

**(ii) Growth of a foetus: ultrasound.** Ultrasound is **non-ionising**, so it does not damage the rapidly dividing cells of the foetus, unlike X-rays, which are ionising and could cause mutations. Pulses of ultrasound are reflected at the boundaries between tissues of different densities (the foetus, the amniotic fluid); the echoes are processed to give a real-time image of the foetus, its size and growth, and the scan can be repeated safely.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the full meaning of ECG?
questions.corrige_markdown: **ECG** stands for **electrocardiogram** (the record produced by an electrocardiograph): a graph of the small potential differences produced by the electrical activity of the heart, measured by electrodes on the skin, against time. It is used to check the rhythm and the health of the heart.
